goal: ga's gemini prompts are compiled from a prompt-spec/1 file with rlo.pspec. Verbatim mode is byte-identical to today's text. Compact mode is used on follow-up turns, including hosts without --resume (agy) that today resend protocol() and the task every turn. A token report shows the saving, and the answer check from the same spec agrees with check_plan.
why: POL-2 T2, CMD-AO3 rev 4 S3 (BD-288 to BD-292). The goal is fewer tokens for the same checked output. T1 succeeded (BD-292): rlo-sdk 6bc76c7 (0.9.0) ships rlo.pspec. Baseline's prototype measured an 8-turn conversation at Gemini 646 -> 447 and agy 2263 -> 1574 tokens (bytes/4 estimate) on ga's own prompts. rev 2 (BD-294): the user turned on billing for the Gemini key, so ga's free-tier default goes too.

scope.text: Move ga's rlo-sdk pin from c491e96 to 6bc76c7 (0.9.0) in every place ga writes it, as in GA25. If a pin lives in GR's files, say so in the report instead of editing it. Later, when baseline judges CMD-K16, AO tells you the K16 sha on this issue and you move the pin once more.

Add ga's gemini prompt spec as a *.pspec file in ga-sdk. Start from baseline's ops/pspec/gemini-plan.pspec. It covers protocol(), the first turn, the --resume turn and the no---resume (agy) turn. ga/gemini.py compiles these prompts with rlo.pspec instead of str.format. In verbatim mode every prompt is byte-identical to today's text.

Compact mode is used on follow-up turns, including hosts without --resume. Verbatim stays selectable (config or flag) for comparison and fallback. Keep the first turn verbatim, and report its compact numbers as a Proposal; baseline decides.

The answer check comes from the same spec. Keep check_plan as the authority in the runtime path. Add tests that the spec's check agrees with check_plan on the 17 cases of baseline ops/pspec/run.py at 7dc9d13. On 6bc76c7 the self-reference case disagrees (16/17); after the K16 pin it must be 17/17. Do not skip or xfail it: report 16/17 with the reason until the pin moves.

A token report, offline and with no model calls required: tokens per turn, verbatim against compact, on a fixed set of at least 8 recorded or labelled turns for each host type (--resume and agy). Show that the same-spec check accepts the well-formed answers of those turns. A real-model comparison is optional and runs only under the integrating side's limits. The changed prompt lands as a normal code diff for a baseline verdict and is never deployed by itself.

BD-294: remove ga/gemini.py DAILY_DEFAULT = {"requests": 20}, which mirrors the old free tier. With no config there is no daily cap; a daily cap applies only when the integrating side configures one (BD-289). The per-minute Governor stays, because it prevents 429s, and its value comes from config. Update any docs or messages that say 20 a day. Do not touch keys or billing.

done_when.text: Verbatim is byte-identical to today's protocol(), first, --resume turn and agy turn, with at least 3 tool tables, against fixtures taken from ga-sdk 438a34a. A mutation that changes one byte in the spec is killed.

The token report for at least 8 turns per host type, verbatim against compact, is no worse than the prototype's 447 (Gemini) and 1574 (agy) on the same conversation. A mutation that resends once-sections in compact on a follow-up turn is killed.

Check agreement on the 17 cases: 17/17 on the K16 pin (16/17 on 6bc76c7, with the self-reference case named). An empty venv installs ga-sdk with the new rlo pin and gives a clean pip check. The full ga suite, GR's tests included, passes in a fresh clone. Report as report/2 in English on #12 with the commit sha.

With no config, ga gemini sets no daily request cap: a test shows that the 21st request in a day is not refused by ga. A configured daily cap is still enforced, and the per-minute Governor still works. Mutations killed: default daily cap restored, and configured cap ignored. Report D1 to D4 together on the K16 pin (3e68f21) as one report/2 on #12.

changes.text: no daily cap unless configured; the per-minute Governor stays
